title: Cloud platform selection
transcript:
Platform Engineering Lead: Alright, let's dive into our cloud provider discussions. We've been considering Google Cloud Platform, Microsoft Azure, and IBM Cloud.

SRE: I've been having some reservations about the potential challenges in integrating Google Cloud with our current infrastructure.

Finance Partner: I've been looking at the financials, and I have to say, Google's per-unit pricing is significantly higher than AWS.

CTO: That's a valid concern, SRE. But let's not forget about Azure. I've done some research, and it seems to have less favorable feature fit for our specific use cases.

Platform Engineering Lead: Agreed, Azure doesn't seem to offer the same level of integration with our existing data analytics stack as AWS.

Finance Partner: But isn't AWS more expensive in the long run due to the higher initial costs?

Platform Engineering Lead: While AWS may have higher initial costs, it offers a more cost-effective long-term solution due to a lower per-unit rate.

SRE: That's true, but we should also consider the potential challenges in integrating AWS with our current infrastructure.

CTO: I understand the concerns, but AWS has committed to offering ongoing support, even given our national charity status.

Finance Partner: Still, I can't help but worry about the long-term financial implications of adopting AWS.

Platform Engineering Lead: I hear your concerns, Finance Partner. However, I believe we can negotiate a flexible payment plan with AWS to better align with our financial limitations.

SRE: Alright, I'll work on mapping out the integration process. But we need to ensure a smooth transition from our current provider, which will take at least 4 months.

CTO: That sounds reasonable. In that case, let's decide to adopt AWS as our primary cloud platform provider.

Finance Partner: I suppose it's the best option we have, given the circumstances. But we need to keep a close eye on the financials.

Platform Engineering Lead: Understood. I'll own this decision and ensure a smooth transition. CTO, would you sign off?

CTO: Yes, decided. Adopt AWS as our primary cloud platform provider.

(Off-topic exchange, not related to the discussion)

Finance Partner: Say, have you tried that new coffee shop downtown? I heard their lattes are excellent.

Platform Engineering Lead: I haven't had the chance yet, but I'll make sure to check it out soon.

(Back to the discussion)

CTO: Alright, let's get to work. Platform Engineering Lead, you're on it. Let's ensure we negotiate a flexible payment plan with AWS and have a smooth transition.

Title: Adoption of AWS as Primary Cloud Platform Provider

Following a comprehensive review, it was decided to adopt Amazon Web Services (AWS) as our primary cloud platform provider. This choice, while involving higher initial costs due to a lower per-unit rate over the long term, was deemed more cost-effective. AWS offers superior integration with our existing data analytics stack and has committed to providing ongoing support, recognizing our status as a national charity. A flexible payment plan with AWS will be negotiated to accommodate our financial limitations. Transition from the current provider, anticipated to take at least 4 months, will be ensured.
